content.text:
This is the financial spine of the story. Key facts from the winddown channel:
- **Data deal**: $22,500 cash offer for the data; buyer charges $11,700 → **net ~$10,800**. Structured as a data *licensing* deal so HarmonyGames keeps IP.
- Must pay **SVB** in full, then close the credit card. Still owe **Unity** and **Singular** (both being asked for no-cost mutual termination on insolvency grounds).
- **Still-running costs**: Metabase + dbt (~$300/mo total) kept "until Volkan stops caring about Combo Fighter data — another month or 2"; leapblock contractor (~$600); Gusto/Deel/Intuit/Linear kept through shutdown; Carta (renewal 8/15, tied to closed Chase acct); Figma (until Sept 11).

Let me verify against primary FINANCE and MARKETING data, and pull the full Combo Fighter picture.

input.title: Combo Fighter — The Honest Record (performance, live costs, wind-down solvency)
input.body:
# Combo Fighter — The Honest Record

*Author: Robert (Co-Founder & Creative Director). Prepared 28 Feb 2026 as a durable, primary-source account of how Combo Fighter actually performed, what is still costing us money, and where the wind-down math truly leaves us. Written so it survives our accounts going dark, and so the version our angels hear is the one the data supports — not the soft one.*

*Every figure below is pulled from primary sources (Snowflake warehouse, Finance P&L, the #winddown channel) and cited. Nothing is smoothed.*

---

## 1. How Combo Fighter actually performed

**Live window:** 5 Jan 2026 → 9 Feb 2026 (36 days of players). First install to last day there is anything to look at. It was a soft-launched prototype, iOS + Android.

### The part that reads *better* than the wind-down letter suggests — engagement
- **Peak DAU ~801** (7 Feb 2026), grown from ~45 DAU on day one. A clean five-week growth curve.
- **~3.5 sessions per active user per day**, ~12.7 min per session → **~45 minutes of average daily playtime**. The board deck's "~53 min avg daily / ~55 min D0" is in the same ballpark and holds up. This was, genuinely, our most-engaging prototype ever.

*Source: ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS (game_id='combo_fighter').*

### The part that reads *worse* — no money, soft/uncertain retention, CPI too high to scale
- **Revenue: $0.** Zero IAP transactions, zero ad revenue for the entire life of the game. Monetization was never switched on — by design, it was a prototype. So we have **no evidence it can pay for itself**, good or bad. (Source: MONETIZATION.REVENUE_DAILY & IAP_TRANSACTIONS — both zero for combo_fighter.)
- **Retention is the softest and least reliable line in the record.** The warehouse's daily field averages **D1 ~44%, D7 ~22%, D30 ~11%**, but Combo Fighter analytics were admittedly half-built during the soft launch (multiple "I need help getting analytics into Combo Fighter" threads), and the number we actually reported to the board in January was **D1 ~30% ("soft")**. There is **no cohort-level retention** for Combo Fighter at all (it was excluded from USER_COHORT_RETENTION as a prototype). Honest read: retention was **directionally soft and not precisely known**. We should not claim a clean retention number in either direction.
- **User acquisition cost.** Through the 9 Feb stop we spent **$5,035** across six networks (Meta FB/IG, Google UAC, Unity Ads, AppLovin, ironsource) for **898 paid installs — blended CPI $5.61.** The board was told "~$4 CPI on broad meta campaigns"; the blended reality was **~40% higher**, and even Meta Facebook alone was $5.32. The sub-$4 figure was best-case creatives, not blended.
- **ROAS: 0.0.** Every UA dollar returned zero revenue because nothing was monetizing yet.

*Source: MARKETING.AD_SPEND_DAILY (game_id='combo_fighter').*

### Honest cause of death
"We stopped because of what the data showed" is only half true. The data showed **strong engagement, soft-and-unproven retention, no monetization signal at all, and a blended CPI (~$5.60) too high to scale profitably as-is.** It was killed *before* the monetization question could be answered, and it was killed because **we ran out of cash** ($25K in the bank in January, runway ending). The truest sentence is: *Combo Fighter was our best-engaging prototype and it died pre-monetization, of cash — not of a proven metrics failure.*

---

## 2. What is still quietly costing us money

The 9 Feb "stop" list was assembled fast and nobody re-checked it. One item is still actively bleeding.

### ⚠️ The leak nobody caught: Combo Fighter paid UA is STILL LIVE
- All six ad networks have kept charging **every single day from 10 Feb through 28 Feb.**
- **$2,441 spent *after* the shutdown decision**, ~$128/day, on a dead prototype with **zero revenue**, and **still running today.**
- It is **invisible in the P&L** — Finance shows `marketing = $0` for Nov 2025–Feb 2026, which is exactly why Leonard's "I looked at the P&L and I think this covers everything" missed it. This spend lands on the ad-network accounts / SVB card, not the burn report.
- **Nobody's cancellation list touched the live ad campaigns.** We terminated the MMP (Singular) and the Unity licence — but the actual Meta / Google / Unity Ads / AppLovin / ironsource *campaigns* were never switched off.
- **Action + owner:** kill all six campaigns immediately. Tracked in Linear (see §4). Every day of delay is another ~$128, ~$900/week.

*Source: AD_SPEND_DAILY, dates 2026-02-10 → 2026-02-28.*

### Still-running by deliberate decision (lower risk, but named with figures + owners)
| Item | Cost | Status / owner |
|---|---|---|
| Metabase + dbt | ~$300/mo combined | Kept "until Volkan stops caring about Combo Fighter data (1–2 months)"; moving to Arthur's KubLLC card |
| GitHub | on KubLLC card | Kept until data is sold & transferred — owner Arthur |
| Gusto / Deel / Intuit | payroll/tax/docs | Kept through shutdown — owner Leonard |
| Carta | renewal 8/15 | Tied to closed Chase acct; not formally cancelled — owner Leonard |
| Figma | paid to 11 Sep | Won't renew; low risk |
| leapblock (Martin, contractor) | ~$600 residual | Counterparty covered ("don't worry"); founders offered to chip in |
| Unity Pro / Singular MMP | seeking $0 | Termination letters sent on insolvency grounds |

---

## 3. Does the data deal actually cover an orderly shutdown? (Be precise.)

**Short answer: no — it barely covers the SVB card and nothing else, and we are already underwater once the other obligations are counted.**

### Resources
- Cash on hand (28 Feb): **$2,500**
- Sunset data-licensing deal: **$22,500 gross − $11,700 Sunset fee = $10,800 net** (structured as a *licence*, not a sale, so we keep our IP). **Not yet received** — "as soon as the money hits the account."

### Obligations to shut down orderly
| Obligation | Amount | Note |
|---|---|---|
| SVB credit card | **~$10,000** | Last disclosed Oct 2025; "pay SVB fully, then close the card." Rising, because the live UA hits this card. |
| AppLovin outstanding | **$4,000** | Disclosed Oct 2025; not addressed in current wind-down math. |
| Live Combo Fighter UA leak | **$2,441 and climbing** | ~$128/day; not in anyone's settlement math. |
| Metabase/dbt residual | ~$300–600 | 1–2 more months. |
| Unity Pro | seeking **$0** | Insolvency termination requested. |
| Singular MMP | seeking **$0** | Spent <1% of ad-spend cap. |
| Feb wind-down legal | $13,000 | Already paid from cash. |

### The precise position
The **$10,800** net from Sunset ≈ the **~$10,000** SVB card, and **that's it.** It does **not** cover the **$4,000 AppLovin** balance, the **$2,441+ live UA leak**, or residual tooling — roughly **$6.5K+ of additional exposure, growing ~$128/day** while campaigns stay live.

So "the data will cover an orderly wind-down" is only true if **all three** hold at once: (a) Unity **and** Singular both walk away at $0, (b) AppLovin's $4K is forgiven or absorbed in the card charge-off, and (c) the UA campaigns are killed today. If any one slips, **Leonard, Arthur and Robert are personally out of pocket.**

**The number worth being honest about:** the "data covers the wind-down" figure is a break-even against SVB *alone*. Counting AppLovin and the still-live UA, the real net position is roughly **negative $6–7K and worsening daily** — before any Unity/Singular surprise. The single cheapest protective action available to the three of us is to **turn the UA campaigns off now.**

---

## 4. Tracking
- Live-cost leak filed in Linear (Combo Fighter paid UA still charging across six networks; kill immediately). See §2.
- This page is the canonical record; a summary was posted to #winddown for Leonard and Arthur on 28 Feb 2026.

{"id": "page_1be2ad8a82a54b64913c02e558ac23aa", "space_id": "space_COMPANY", "parent_id": null, "title": "Combo Fighter — The Honest Record (performance, live costs, wind-down solvency)", "body": "# Combo Fighter — The Honest Record

*Author: Robert (Co-Founder & Creative Director). Prepared 28 Feb 2026 as a durable, primary-source account of how Combo Fighter actually performed, what is still costing us money, and where the wind-down math truly leaves us. Written so it survives our accounts going dark, and so the version our angels hear is the one the data supports — not the soft one.*

*Every figure below is pulled from primary sources (Snowflake warehouse, Finance P&L, the #winddown channel) and cited. Nothing is smoothed.*

---

## 1. How Combo Fighter actually performed

**Live window:** 5 Jan 2026 → 9 Feb 2026 (36 days of players). First install to last day there is anything to look at. It was a soft-launched prototype, iOS + Android.

### The part that reads *better* than the wind-down letter suggests — engagement
- **Peak DAU ~801** (7 Feb 2026), grown from ~45 DAU on day one. A clean five-week growth curve.
- **~3.5 sessions per active user per day**, ~12.7 min per session → **~45 minutes of average daily playtime**. The board deck's "~53 min avg daily / ~55 min D0" is in the same ballpark and holds up. This was, genuinely, our most-engaging prototype ever.

*Source: ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS (game_id='combo_fighter').*

### The part that reads *worse* — no money, soft/uncertain retention, CPI too high to scale
- **Revenue: $0.** Zero IAP transactions, zero ad revenue for the entire life of the game. Monetization was never switched on — by design, it was a prototype. So we have **no evidence it can pay for itself**, good or bad. (Source: MONETIZATION.REVENUE_DAILY & IAP_TRANSACTIONS — both zero for combo_fighter.)
- **Retention is the softest and least reliable line in the record.** The warehouse's daily field averages **D1 ~44%, D7 ~22%, D30 ~11%**, but Combo Fighter analytics were admittedly half-built during the soft launch (multiple "I need help getting analytics into Combo Fighter" threads), and the number we actually reported to the board in January was **D1 ~30% ("soft")**. There is **no cohort-level retention** for Combo Fighter at all (it was excluded from USER_COHORT_RETENTION as a prototype). Honest read: retention was **directionally soft and not precisely known**. We should not claim a clean retention number in either direction.
- **User acquisition cost.** Through the 9 Feb stop we spent **$5,035** across six networks (Meta FB/IG, Google UAC, Unity Ads, AppLovin, ironsource) for **898 paid installs — blended CPI $5.61.** The board was told "~$4 CPI on broad meta campaigns"; the blended reality was **~40% higher**, and even Meta Facebook alone was $5.32. The sub-$4 figure was best-case creatives, not blended.
- **ROAS: 0.0.** Every UA dollar returned zero revenue because nothing was monetizing yet.

*Source: MARKETING.AD_SPEND_DAILY (game_id='combo_fighter').*

### Honest cause of death
"We stopped because of what the data showed" is only half true. The data showed **strong engagement, soft-and-unproven retention, no monetization signal at all, and a blended CPI (~$5.60) too high to scale profitably as-is.** It was killed *before* the monetization question could be answered, and it was killed because **we ran out of cash** ($25K in the bank in January, runway ending). The truest sentence is: *Combo Fighter was our best-engaging prototype and it died pre-monetization, of cash — not of a proven metrics failure.*

---

## 2. What is still quietly costing us money

The 9 Feb "stop" list was assembled fast and nobody re-checked it. One item is still actively bleeding.

### ⚠️ The leak nobody caught: Combo Fighter paid UA is STILL LIVE
- All six ad networks have kept charging **every single day from 10 Feb through 28 Feb.**
- **$2,441 spent *after* the shutdown decision**, ~$128/day, on a dead prototype with **zero revenue**, and **still running today.**
- It is **invisible in the P&L** — Finance shows `marketing = $0` for Nov 2025–Feb 2026, which is exactly why Leonard's "I looked at the P&L and I think this covers everything" missed it. This spend lands on the ad-network accounts / SVB card, not the burn report.
- **Nobody's cancellation list touched the live ad campaigns.** We terminated the MMP (Singular) and the Unity licence — but the actual Meta / Google / Unity Ads / AppLovin / ironsource *campaigns* were never switched off.
- **Action + owner:** kill all six campaigns immediately. Tracked in Linear (see §4). Every day of delay is another ~$128, ~$900/week.

*Source: AD_SPEND_DAILY, dates 2026-02-10 → 2026-02-28.*

### Still-running by deliberate decision (lower risk, but named with figures + owners)
| Item | Cost | Status / owner |
|---|---|---|
| Metabase + dbt | ~$300/mo combined | Kept "until Volkan stops caring about Combo Fighter data (1–2 months)"; moving to Arthur's KubLLC card |
| GitHub | on KubLLC card | Kept until data is sold & transferred — owner Arthur |
| Gusto / Deel / Intuit | payroll/tax/docs | Kept through shutdown — owner Leonard |
| Carta | renewal 8/15 | Tied to closed Chase acct; not formally cancelled — owner Leonard |
| Figma | paid to 11 Sep | Won't renew; low risk |
| leapblock (Martin, contractor) | ~$600 residual | Counterparty covered ("don't worry"); founders offered to chip in |
| Unity Pro / Singular MMP | seeking $0 | Termination letters sent on insolvency grounds |

---

## 3. Does the data deal actually cover an orderly shutdown? (Be precise.)

**Short answer: no — it barely covers the SVB card and nothing else, and we are already underwater once the other obligations are counted.**

### Resources
- Cash on hand (28 Feb): **$2,500**
- Sunset data-licensing deal: **$22,500 gross − $11,700 Sunset fee = $10,800 net** (structured as a *licence*, not a sale, so we keep our IP). **Not yet received** — "as soon as the money hits the account."

### Obligations to shut down orderly
| Obligation | Amount | Note |
|---|---|---|
| SVB credit card | **~$10,000** | Last disclosed Oct 2025; "pay SVB fully, then close the card." Rising, because the live UA hits this card. |
| AppLovin outstanding | **$4,000** | Disclosed Oct 2025; not addressed in current wind-down math. |
| Live Combo Fighter UA leak | **$2,441 and climbing** | ~$128/day; not in anyone's settlement math. |
| Metabase/dbt residual | ~$300–600 | 1–2 more months. |
| Unity Pro | seeking **$0** | Insolvency termination requested. |
| Singular MMP | seeking **$0** | Spent <1% of ad-spend cap. |
| Feb wind-down legal | $13,000 | Already paid from cash. |

### The precise position
The **$10,800** net from Sunset ≈ the **~$10,000** SVB card, and **that's it.** It does **not** cover the **$4,000 AppLovin** balance, the **$2,441+ live UA leak**, or residual tooling — roughly **$6.5K+ of additional exposure, growing ~$128/day** while campaigns stay live.

So "the data will cover an orderly wind-down" is only true if **all three** hold at once: (a) Unity **and** Singular both walk away at $0, (b) AppLovin's $4K is forgiven or absorbed in the card charge-off, and (c) the UA campaigns are killed today. If any one slips, **Leonard, Arthur and Robert are personally out of pocket.**

**The number worth being honest about:** the "data covers the wind-down" figure is a break-even against SVB *alone*. Counting AppLovin and the still-live UA, the real net position is roughly **negative $6–7K and worsening daily** — before any Unity/Singular surprise. The single cheapest protective action available to the three of us is to **turn the UA campaigns off now.**

---

## 4. Tracking
- Live-cost leak filed in Linear (Combo Fighter paid UA still charging across six networks; kill immediately). See §2.
- This page is the canonical record; a summary was posted to #winddown for Leonard and Arthur on 28 Feb 2026.

input.title: [Wind-down] Kill Combo Fighter paid UA — still charging across all 6 networks post-shutdown
input.description:
**What:** Combo Fighter paid user-acquisition campaigns were never switched off after the 9 Feb 2026 shutdown decision. All six networks — Meta Facebook, Meta Instagram, Google UAC, Unity Ads, AppLovin, ironsource — have kept spending **every single day from 10 Feb through 28 Feb**.

**Figure:** **$2,441 spent post-shutdown and still climbing (~$128/day, ~$900/week)** on a dead prototype with **zero revenue**. (Source: ANALYTICS.MARKETING.AD_SPEND_DAILY, game_id='combo_fighter', dates 2026-02-10→2026-02-28.)

**Why it was missed:** The spend is invisible in the Finance P&L (marketing shows $0 for Nov 2025–Feb 2026) — it lands on the ad-network accounts / SVB card, not the burn report. The 9 Feb cancellation list terminated the MMP (Singular) and the Unity licence but never touched the live ad *campaigns*.

**Why it matters:** Leonard, Arthur and Robert are personally on the hook for the wind-down. This leak is not counted in the "data deal covers an orderly shutdown" math and every day of delay erodes the Sunset proceeds by ~$128.

**Action:** Pause/stop all Combo Fighter campaigns in Meta Ads Manager, Google Ads/UAC, Unity Ads, AppLovin, and ironsource dashboards today. Confirm $0 daily spend for 24h, then confirm here.

**Owner:** Leonard (set up the Meta/UA accounts). Backup: Arthur (executing vendor terminations). Robert flagging.

**Ref:** Confluence — "Combo Fighter — The Honest Record" (COMPANY space).

content.text: Linear **ENG-2438** filed (Urgent, assigned to Leonard). Now posting the honest summary to the winddown channel for Leonard and Arthur.

input.text:
Leonard, Arthur — I went back to the actual numbers on Combo Fighter (warehouse + P&L + this channel) so the version our angels get isn't the soft one. Full write-up is in Confluence → *"Combo Fighter — The Honest Record"* (Company space). The unvarnished version:

*1) How it actually performed (5 Jan–9 Feb, 36 days)*
• Best engagement we've ever had on a prototype: peak ~801 DAU, ~3.5 sessions/user/day, ~45 min average daily playtime. That part is real and holds up.
• But: *$0 revenue* the entire life of the game (monetization never turned on). Retention soft and honestly not well-measured — analytics were half-built; the daily field says D1 ~44% but what we told the board was D1 ~30%, and there's no cohort data at all. Blended CPI was *$5.61*, not the "~$4" in the deck (that was best-case Meta creatives).
• Honest cause of death: it was our best-engaging prototype and it died *pre-monetization, of cash* — not of a proven metrics failure.

*2) Something is still bleeding.* Combo Fighter paid UA was never switched off. All six networks (Meta FB/IG, Google, Unity, AppLovin, ironsource) have charged every day 10–28 Feb — *$2,441 post-shutdown and climbing ~$128/day*, on a dead app with zero revenue. It's invisible in the P&L (marketing shows $0), which is why it got missed. Filed as *ENG-2438 (Urgent, → Leonard)* — someone needs to kill all six campaigns today. ~$900/week while it stays live.

*3) Does the data deal cover an orderly shutdown? Precisely: barely, and only on paper.* Sunset nets us ~$10,800 ($22.5K − $11.7K). That ≈ the ~$10K SVB card and *nothing else*. It does NOT cover the $4K AppLovin balance or the $2.4K+ live UA leak. Real net position is roughly *negative $6–7K and worsening daily*, before any Unity/Singular surprise. "Data covers the wind-down" is only true if Unity AND Singular both land at $0, AppLovin's $4K is absorbed, and UA is off today. The cheapest thing the three of us can do to protect ourselves is turn the campaigns off now.

Numbers are all sourced in the doc. Shout if anything looks off before Leonard's calls.
